facts.statement: Adeopapposaurus is a genus of plateosaurian dinosaur with a long neck, meaning "far eating lizard".
facts.quote: Adeopapposaurus (meaning "far eating lizard", in reference to its long neck) is a genus of plateosaurian dinosaur

facts.statement: The dinosaur Adeopapposaurus was described in 2009 by paleontologist Ricardo N. Martínez.
facts.quote: Adeopapposaurus was described in 2009 by Ricardo N. Martínez.

facts.statement: Scientists know of four partial skeletons and two partial skulls of Adeopapposaurus.
facts.quote: Four partial skeletons with two partial skulls are known.

facts.statement: Bone structure at the jaw tips suggests Adeopapposaurus possessed keratinous beaks.
facts.quote: The form of the bones at the tips of the upper and lower jaws suggests it had keratinous beaks.

facts.statement: Adeopapposaurus is classified within the family Massospondylidae.
facts.quote: Adeopapposaurus is classified as a massospondylid.

facts.statement: Adeopapposaurus lived between 201.4 and 174.7 million years ago during the Hettangian to Toarcian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Toarcian (201.4 to 174.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Adeopapposaurus is the family Massospondylidae.

rejected.statement: Fossils of Adeopapposaurus were found in the Early Jurassic Cañón del Colorado Formation in San Juan, Argentina.
rejected.quote: Adeopapposaurus ... from the Early Jurassic Cañón del Colorado Formation of San Juan, Argentina.
